Botnet_ARES.description: Traffic from compromised devices controlled remotely by an attacker, often an IoT botnet using encrypted communication.
mitigation: Patch IoT devices and change default credentials.
Segment IoT devices on a separate network.
Monitor outbound traffic for unusual destinations or periodic check-ins.

DDoS_LOIT.description: Distributed denial-of-service attack using the Low Orbit Ion Cannon tool to flood a target with TCP, UDP, or HTTP requests.
mitigation: Use a DDoS-protection service or upstream scrubbing centre.
Rate-limit incoming connections at the network edge.
Enable SYN-cookies and connection limits on public servers.

DoS_GoldenEye.description: Single-source denial-of-service attack using the GoldenEye tool, often sending HTTP GET/POST floods and slow-connection attacks.
mitigation: Deploy a web application firewall with rate-limiting rules.
Set strict HTTP connection timeout values.
Use load balancers that can absorb short bursts.

DoS_Hulk.description: High-volume HTTP flood attack that overwhelms a web server with many unique or obfuscated requests.
mitigation: Rate-limit requests per IP address.
Use a web application firewall to block malformed or repetitive HTTP patterns.
Auto-scale web servers to handle unexpected spikes.

DoS_Slowhttptest.description: Slow denial-of-service attack that keeps many connections open by sending HTTP headers very slowly, exhausting server connection pools.
mitigation: Lower HTTP keep-alive timeouts and maximum connection limits.
Use a reverse proxy that can buffer slow clients.
Monitor for many incomplete HTTP requests.

DoS_Slowloris.description: Slow denial-of-service attack that opens many connections and sends partial HTTP headers slowly, blocking legitimate users.
mitigation: Configure web servers to close idle connections quickly.
Limit concurrent connections per IP address.
Use a web application firewall or load balancer with slow-attack protection.

FTP-Patator.description: Brute-force attack that repeatedly tries username/password combinations against an FTP service.
mitigation: Enforce strong passwords and account lockout after failed attempts.
Disable FTP where possible and use SFTP or FTPS instead.
Monitor FTP logs for many failed login attempts.

Heartbleed.description: Exploitation of the Heartbleed bug in OpenSSL to read sensitive server memory, including private keys.
mitigation: Patch OpenSSL immediately.
Replace SSL certificates and private keys that may have been exposed.
Use vulnerability scanners to confirm no unpatched services remain.

Port_Scan.description: Automated scanning of a network to discover open ports and running services, often a precursor to an attack.
mitigation: Use a firewall to block unsolicited connection attempts.
Deploy an intrusion-detection system that alerts on sequential port probes.
Close unnecessary ports and services on all hosts.

SSH-Patator.description: Brute-force attack against SSH login, trying many username/password pairs to break into a system.
mitigation: Disable password-based SSH login and use key-based authentication.
Change the SSH port from the default 22 as a minor deterrent.
Use fail2ban or similar tools to block IPs after repeated failures.

Web_Brute_Force.description: Automated guessing of login credentials on a web application authentication form.
mitigation: Add CAPTCHA or rate-limiting to login pages.
Enforce account lockout after a small number of failed attempts.
Use multi-factor authentication for user accounts.

Web_SQL_Injection.description: Attacker inserts malicious SQL code into input fields to manipulate or extract data from a backend database.
mitigation: Use parameterised queries or prepared statements in application code.
Validate and sanitise all user input on the server side.
Deploy a web application firewall with SQL-injection rules and run vulnerability scans.

Web_XSS.description: Cross-site scripting attack where malicious JavaScript is injected into a web page and executed in other users' browsers.
mitigation: Encode output and validate input to prevent script injection.
Implement a Content-Security-Policy header.
Keep web frameworks and libraries up to date, and use a web application firewall to block common XSS patterns.
